in_english.name: Eugenio
in_english.long_meaning: Eugenio (Eugenio) is derived from the Greek (eugénēs) meaning good (good) or noble (noble) and well-born (well-born) . In the Bible, (eugénēs) is used to describe someone who is well-born or of noble descent (Genesis 41:45) . In Christian tradition, the name Eugenio is often associated with (Iēsous) (Jesus) and (Nikolaos) (Nicholas) . The name is also found in the writings of (Iēsous) (Jesus) as recorded in the (Baptistēs) (Baptist) . In modern times, the name Eugenio is often used in Christian cultures to signify a person who is well-born or of noble character .

data.cultural_impact: The name Eugenio holds a significant cultural impact in the Hispanic community, as it was a common name for noblemen and nobility throughout history. This legacy continues in Latin America, where the name is still popular. Additionally, in some countries such as Spain, Eugenio is a variant of the name Eugenius, which was the name of several Roman emperors, adding to its prestigious historical significance.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian context, the name Eugenio holds a significant spiritual significance as it is the name of several saints and martyrs. One of the most notable is Saint Eugenio of Toledo, a bishop and martyr who was venerated for his steadfastness and devotion to his faith. Eugenio de Palacio y Zardáñas, a Spanish Basque theologian and priest, is also known for his profound religious and intellectual contributions. The name Eugenio, then, embodies purity, faith, and strength, reminding us of the virtues we should strive to cultivate in ourselves.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Eugenio: From the Greek name Eugenios, meaning “well-born” or “noble” in origin, symbolizing the potential for spiritual nobility and excellence in all Christians, as children of God.

historical_references.reference: Saint Eugenius of Carthage, a bishop who was martyred during the Diocletian persecution (AD 303-311). He was known for his miracles and was particularly renowned for his role in the conversion of a group of Donatist heretics.
historical_references.context: Religious persecution under Roman Emperor Diocletian and the conversion of Donatist heretics.

historical_references.reference: Pope Eugenius III (1145-1153), who issued the first papal bull authorizing a crusade against the Muslim rulers of Sicily and Africa, marking a significant shift in the focus of the Crusades from the Holy Land to the Mediterranean.
historical_references.context: Papal decree for a crusade against Muslim rulers in Sicily and Africa.
